chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather, al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: Jibra'il came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Blessed is he from among your Ummah who says: There is no god but Allah, Alone, Alone, Alone.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (Declaration of Monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who sincerely profess monotheism according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* underscores the eschatological joy (*tuba*) for those who affirm divine unity with profound emphasis, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Tawhid* as the foundation of faith. The repetition of 'wahduhu' (His oneness) in the narration highlights the intensity of conviction required, linking the declaration of faith directly to angelic witness and divine pleasure. It serves as a theological anchor for the Shia understanding that correct belief (*aqidah*) is intrinsically tied to spiritual reward.
